narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California recorded $1.2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Regents of the University of California secured 3 awards so far, with an average award size of $410M. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year. Department of Energy is the dominant buyer, accounting for $1.2B in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the largest market, with $1.2B in obligations. Smaller FY2026 to date activity includes $4M in Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools and $31.3K in Computer Facilities Management Services. Historical fiscal-year obligations show large swings: FY21 was $67.4M, FY22 was $6.7M, FY23 was $982M, FY24 was $1.4B, FY25 was $1.3B, and FY26 is $1.2B to date. Use these figures when sizing opportunities, prioritizing outreach, or benchmarking Regents of the University of California against peer research-focused contractors.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Regents of the University of California's federal obligations?
sections.body: Department of Energy accounts for the vast majority of FY2026 to date obligations at $1.2B. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounts for $1.2B of obligations, indicating concentration in a single market and buyer. Smaller markets and agencies include Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Department of Commerce at $31.3K.

sections.heading: How has Regents of the University of California's federal buying trended since FY21?
sections.body: Obligations rose from $67.4M in FY21 to $982M in FY23, then peaked at $1.4B in FY24 before falling to $1.3B in FY25 and $1.2B in FY26 to date. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year between FY25 and FY26 to date. Award activity in FY2026 to date shows 3 awards with an average award size of $410M.

faq.q: How much does Regents of the University of California make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has received $1.2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Regents of the University of California has 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $410M, and obligations fell 5.9% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Regents of the University of California?
faq.a: Department of Energy buys from Regents of the University of California, with $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. Department of Commerce also appears as a buyer with $31.3K in obligations.

faq.q: What does Regents of the University of California sell to the government?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California sells research and development services, reflected by $1.2B in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences obligations in FY2026 to date. Regents of the University of California also records $4M for Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools and $31.3K for Computer Facilities Management Services.

faq.a: No Regents of the University of California contracts are listed as expiring soon. No expiring-contract entries are reported for FY2026 to date.
